note: The Isle of Man's visitors meet the United Kingdom's visa requirements (its Immigration Service sends them to GOV.UK's check, and a UK visa admits them), and its own ETA scheme, legally distinct but mirroring the UK's: the gb list.

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Immigration: Visit
sources.said: Holders of a valid visa for the UK or the Channel Islands can travel freely around the Common Travel Area without the need for applying for a specific visa for the Isle of Man. Nationals of certain countries do not need to apply for entry clearance prior to travel to the Isle of Man/United Kingdom. Instead they are assessed at the point of entry into the United Kingdom.

sources.title: Home Office, Common Travel Area guidance (GOV.UK)
sources.said: Each CTA jurisdiction is largely responsible for decisions on who can enter and stay. The Crown Dependencies have almost identical visa requirements to that of the UK. ... Each Crown Dependency (Jersey, Guernsey and Isle of Man) has introduced their own legally distinct ETA schemes.
